newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FACB sees no profit impact from Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: FACB sees no profit impact from Cambodia.

text.p: Malaysian construction firm FACB Bhd, which has investments in Cambodia, said on Friday that the political disruption in the war-torn country would not affect its bottom line for the current financial year.

"If you are referring to the public listed company (FACB), no," said Chen Lip Keong, FACB chief executive when asked whether the company's profits this year would be dented by recent fighting in Cambodia.
Chen, speaking at a groundbreaking for an FACB building, said FACB's total investments in Cambodia amounted to around $50 million.
The company had announced plans last October to build three hotels in Cambodia as part of its Nexus Hotels International chain.
Chen's privately-owned Ariston Group of Companies had said on July 7 that it would not "take any risks" with its employees in the country. Ariston is the largest single foreign investor in Cambodia.
"Lives come first, then money," said Chen on Friday.
Ariston is involved in a $1.3 billion Sihanoukville project involving the redevelopment of the Kang Keng airport, as well as construction of a casino and hotel resort on Naga Island.
Bitter fighting between forces aligned with Cambodia's two feuding prime ministers erupted earlier in July, prompting hundreds of Malaysian companies to evacuate their employees from the country.
Earlier on Friday, Malaysian Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the Cambodian government has assured Malaysia that Malaysian investments were safe.
"I do not see any immediate or long-term difficulty for our investment in Cambodia," Anwar said at the FACB function.
